title: What is a firewall?
summary: Learn what a firewall does, how it filters traffic, and the difference between stateless and stateful firewalls.

blocks.text: A **firewall** sits between networks and decides which traffic is allowed through.

blocks.description: A firewall placed between the internet and an internal network, with arrows showing allowed and blocked traffic.
blocks.caption: A firewall filters traffic between networks

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: A **stateful** firewall tracks connections. A **stateless** firewall checks each packet on its own.

cards.back: Checks each packet against rules without remembering earlier packets.
Tracks the state of connections and allows replies to approved requests.

blocks.situation: An external host sends unexpected traffic to port 3389 on an internal server.
blocks.question: What should the firewall do by default?

options.text: Allow it, since it might be useful
options.feedback: A default-deny approach blocks traffic that is not explicitly allowed.

options.text: Block it unless a rule allows it
options.feedback: Correct. Default deny is the safer approach.

items: A firewall filters traffic using rules
Default deny is the safer approach

imageBriefs.brief: Simple diagram: internet on the left, firewall in the middle, internal network on the right, with arrows for allowed and blocked traffic.
